title: Corporate Leave & Attendance Policy
long_prompt:
NORTHWIND TECHNOLOGIES PRIVATE LIMITED
EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK - REVISED EDITION 2024
SECTION 4: LEAVE AND ATTENDANCE POLICY

4.1 GENERAL PRINCIPLES
All permanent employees of Northwind Technologies Private Limited are eligible for leave as described in this section. Contract employees, interns and consultants are governed by separate agreements and this section does not apply to them. Leave is a privilege granted in accordance with business requirements and is not an accrued right that can be converted to cash except where expressly stated in Section 4.9. Employees are expected to plan their leave in advance and obtain written approval from their reporting manager before booking travel. Retrospective leave applications, except in cases of medical emergency, may be rejected at the discretion of the manager.

4.2 ELIGIBILITY AND ACCRUAL
Permanent employees become eligible for leave only after completion of the probation period of six months from the date of joining. During probation an employee may take up to seven days of leave on a loss of pay basis, subject to manager approval. Upon confirmation, leave accrues on a monthly basis at the rates tabulated below and is credited to the employee leave ledger on the first day of each following calendar month. Accrual is calculated pro rata for employees joining mid-month. Any leave not used by 31 March of each fiscal year lapses, with a maximum carry-forward of ten days into the next fiscal year, and carry-forwarded days must be used within the first quarter of the new fiscal year.

Casual Leave: twelve days per calendar year, accruing at one day per month. Casual leave may be taken in half-day increments and may be clubbed with earned leave. Casual leave cannot be taken on consecutive working days for more than three days at a time, and cannot be combined with sick leave without prior written approval from Human Resources.

Sick Leave: twelve days per calendar year, accruing at one day per month. A medical certificate from a registered medical practitioner is mandatory for any sick leave exceeding two consecutive working days. Employees undergoing planned surgery may apply for extended sick leave of up to thirty days with supporting documentation from a government hospital or a hospital recognised by the company medical board.

Earned Leave: one and a quarter days per calendar month of completed service, that is fifteen days per year. Earned leave is the only category that is encashable, either on separation or on retirement, at the last drawn daily basic salary. Encashment is limited to a maximum of forty-five days in a single instance.

4.3 HOLIDAYS AND WEEKLY OFFS
The company observes fifteen gazetted holidays each year as notified by the HR calendar published every December. In addition, employees are entitled to one weekly off, normally on Sunday, though shift-based roles in the Bengaluru operations centre may have rotational weekly offs as per the shift roster. Festive holidays announced by state or central government after the calendar is published will be treated as holidays by transition and do not require a leave application.

4.4 APPLICATION AND APPROVAL WORKFLOW
Leave must be applied at least five working days in advance on the Oracle Fusion HR portal. Applications less than five working days in advance are treated as urgent applications and require a documented reason. Approval authority is determined by the duration: up to two days is approved by the reporting manager, three to five days by the delivery manager, and more than five days by the Senior Vice President of the business unit along with an HR business partner. Any leave taken without approval, even if applied for later, is treated as unauthorised absence. Three instances of unauthorised absence in a rolling twelve-month period will result in a formal warning, and five instances will result in termination for cause under clause 12.4 of the employment agreement.

4.5 WORK FROM HOME
Work from home is not classified as leave. Employees may work from home up to two days per week with manager approval, provided the role does not require physical presence. Client-facing and lab-based roles are excluded. Work from home beyond two days per week requires a written exception approved by the Human Resources head.

4.6 PATERNITY, MATERNITY AND PARENTAL LEAVE
Female employees are entitled to twenty-six weeks of paid maternity leave as mandated by the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, applicable for the first two surviving children. Male employees are entitled to fifteen days of paid paternity leave, which must be availed within six months of the child's birth. Adoption and surrogacy leave of twelve weeks is available to the commissioning mother.

4.7 UNPAID LEAVE
An employee who has exhausted all credited leave may apply for leave without pay for up to thirty days in a fiscal year, subject to approval by the Senior Vice President. Leave without pay beyond thirty days requires the approval of the Chief People Officer and may affect the annual performance rating.

4.8 COMPENSATORY OFF
Compensatory off may be granted for working on a notified holiday or a weekly off, provided the employee logs the working day on the timesheet within seven days. Compensatory off must be availed within sixty days of being earned, after which it lapses automatically without notice.

4.9 ENCASHMENT AND FINAL SETTLEMENT
On separation, unused earned leave up to forty-five days is encashed. Casual and sick leave are not encashed under any circumstance. Final settlement including encashment is processed within thirty days of the last working day, subject to complete handover and full and final settlement of all company assets.

4.10 ROLE OF THE REPORTING MANAGER
Managers must ensure adequate team coverage during planned absences and must not approve leave that would leave a critical production system without an on-call owner. Managers who approve leave in violation of this clause will be subject to a performance improvement plan.
question: How many days of casual leave does a confirmed employee get per year, what restriction applies to consecutive casual leave, and is casual leave encashable?
reference_answer: A confirmed employee gets twelve days of casual leave per calendar year, accruing at one day per month. Casual leave cannot be taken on consecutive working days for more than three days at a time, and it cannot be combined with sick leave without prior written Human Resources approval. Casual leave is not encashable; only earned leave is encashable, limited to a maximum of forty-five days in a single instance.

title: Cloud Storage Service - Pricing and Limits
long_prompt:
CLOUDVAULT API AND PLAN DOCUMENTATION - EFFECTIVE 01 JANUARY 2025

1. PLAN OVERVIEW
CloudVault offers four plans: Free, Starter, Professional and Enterprise. All plans are billed either monthly or annually, and annual billing receives a discount of twenty percent relative to the monthly rate. Prices quoted are in United States dollars and exclude applicable taxes, duties and value added tax, which will be added at the point of sale. Prices may be revised with thirty days notice communicated to the account owner by email and displayed in the billing console.

1.1 FREE PLAN
The Free plan costs zero dollars and is intended for evaluation. It includes 5 GB of standard storage, 10,000 API requests per month, 1 GB of monthly egress and community support only. A single user seat is included. Objects larger than 5 GB are not supported. Data stored on the Free plan is deleted after ninety days of account inactivity. No service level agreement applies to the Free plan and no uptime guarantee is offered.

1.2 STARTER PLAN
The Starter plan costs 9 dollars per month billed monthly, or 7.20 dollars per month billed annually. It includes 100 GB of standard storage, 100,000 API requests per month, 50 GB of monthly egress, three user seats and email support with a response target of two business days. Versioning is retained for seven days. Cross-region replication is not available on this plan. The maximum object size is 25 GB.

1.3 PROFESSIONAL PLAN
The Professional plan costs 49 dollars per month billed monthly, or 39.20 dollars per month billed annually. It includes 1 TB of standard storage, 2 million API requests per month, 500 GB of monthly egress, twenty user seats, and priority email and chat support with a four hour response target. Versioning is retained for ninety days, cross-region replication is included for one destination region, and the maximum object size is 100 GB. SSO via SAML 2.0, audit logs and role-based access control are included. A 99.9 percent monthly uptime service level agreement applies, with service credits of ten percent of the monthly fee for each full 0.1 percent below the commitment, capped at one hundred percent of the monthly fee.

1.4 ENTERPRISE PLAN
The Enterprise plan is priced by quotation and includes unlimited storage subject to fair use, dedicated support with a one hour response target, a 99.95 percent uptime commitment, unlimited seats, customer managed encryption keys, private networking, two destination regions for replication and a named technical account manager. Enterprise agreements are for a minimum term of twelve months and are non-cancellable.

2. OVERAGE AND METERING
Storage above the plan allowance is charged at 0.023 dollars per GB per month for standard storage and 0.012 dollars per GB per month for infrequent access storage. API requests above the allowance are charged at 0.40 dollars per million requests for reads and 5.00 dollars per million for writes. Egress above the allowance is charged at 0.09 dollars per GB. Metering is performed on a five minute rolling window and billing is calculated daily, aggregated at the end of the billing period. There is no minimum charge and partial GBs are billed to three decimal places.

3. OBJECT AND FILE LIMITS
The maximum object size is plan dependent as stated above. The maximum number of objects per bucket is one million on Free and Starter plans and unlimited on Professional and Enterprise. Directory nesting depth is limited to 64 levels. Metadata per object is limited to 2 KB of user defined keys. Multipart uploads support up to 10,000 parts with a minimum part size of 5 MB, except for the final part which may be smaller.

4. SECURITY AND COMPLIANCE
All data is encrypted in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher and at rest using AES-256. The Professional and Enterprise plans include server side encryption with customer provided keys. CloudVault is certified to ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type II. GDPR data processing agreements are available on all paid plans. The Free plan includes encryption in transit and at rest but does not include customer managed keys or a data processing agreement.

5. SUPPORT
Community support is available through the forum on all plans. Email support is available from the Starter plan. Priority support with a four hour first response target is available on Professional. Dedicated support with a one hour target, telephone escalation and a named account engineer is available only on Enterprise. Support is offered in English and Japanese during business hours in the Americas and Europe time zones.

6. DATA RETENTION AND DELETION
Upon plan downgrade, data above the new storage limit is retained for thirty days and then deleted irreversibly. Upon account cancellation, all data is deleted within seven days, with an optional thirty day grace period available on Professional and Enterprise plans by contacting support. Deleted objects in the recycle bin are retained for the versioning period of the plan.
question: What is the monthly cost of the Professional plan when billed annually, and how does it compare to monthly billing?
reference_answer: The Professional plan costs 49 dollars per month when billed monthly and 39.20 dollars per month when billed annually, because annual billing receives a twenty percent discount. Billed annually it is therefore 9.80 dollars per month cheaper than monthly billing, saving 117.60 dollars over a year.

title: Laptop Hardware Specification and Warranty Terms
long_prompt:
APEXBOOK PRO 14 - TECHNICAL SPECIFICATION AND WARRANTY SCHEDULE
DOCUMENT PART NUMBER APX-14-2024-WR

1. HARDWARE SPECIFICATION
Processor: 14th generation Intel Core Ultra 7 155H, 16 cores (6 performance, 8 efficiency, 2 low power), base power 28 W, maximum turbo power 115 W.
Memory: 16 GB LPDDR5X soldered memory at 7467 MT/s. Memory is not user upgradeable and there are no SO-DIMM slots.
Storage: 512 GB PCIe Gen 4 NVMe M.2 solid state drive, read speeds up to 5000 MB/s and write speeds up to 4200 MB/s. One additional M.2 2280 slot is available and is user accessible by removing the bottom panel.
Display: 14.0 inch OLED, 2880 by 1800 resolution, 16:10 aspect ratio, 120 Hz adaptive refresh rate, 500 nits standard brightness and 600 nits peak brightness, 100 percent DCI-P3 coverage, DisplayHDR True Black 600 certified.
Graphics: integrated Intel Arc graphics with hardware ray tracing support and AV1 encode and decode.
Battery: 75 watt-hour lithium polymer battery. Rated video playback runtime is 14 hours at 150 nits brightness with the display at 60 Hz. Fast charging via the 100 W USB-C power adapter charges the battery from zero to fifty percent in 30 minutes.
Ports: two Thunderbolt 4 USB-C ports supporting power delivery and display port 2.1, one USB-A 3.2 Gen 1 port, one HDMI 2.1 port, one 3.5 mm combo audio jack and a full size SD card reader.
Wireless: Wi-Fi 7 tri-band and Bluetooth 5.4. No Ethernet port is provided; a USB-C adapter is sold separately.
Camera: 1080p infrared camera with a physical electronic privacy shutter and Windows Hello facial recognition.
Audio: quad speaker array with Dolby Atmos support, dual array microphone with artificial intelligence noise cancellation.
Weight: 1.28 kg. Chassis material is CNC machined aluminium with a magnesium alloy internal frame.
Operating system: Windows 11 Home, 64 bit. Windows 11 Pro is available as a paid upgrade at the point of purchase only and cannot be added after delivery.

2. IN THE BOX
Laptop, 100 W USB-C power adapter, USB-C to USB-C cable of 1 metre, quick start guide, warranty card. No mouse, no sleeve and no USB-C to USB-A dongle are included.

3. WARRANTY PERIOD AND COVERAGE
This product carries a limited hardware warranty of thirty six months from the date of original retail purchase, covering parts and labour for repairs performed by authorised service centres. The warranty covers defects in materials and workmanship under normal use in accordance with the user guide. The battery carries a separate warranty of twelve months or three hundred charge cycles, whichever occurs first, and is excluded from the thirty six month coverage. The warranty includes on-site service for the first twelve months in cities where on-site service is available; from month thirteen onwards service is carry-in to the nearest authorised service centre. Shipping to and from the service centre during carry-in service is borne by the customer within the warranty period.

4. WHAT THE WARRANTY DOES NOT COVER
The warranty does not cover damage caused by accident, abuse, misuse, unauthorized modification, liquid contact outside of the rated splash resistance, or damage caused by use of non-approved accessories or power adapters. The warranty is void if the serial number label has been removed or altered, if the bottom panel seal is broken by a person who is not an authorised technician, or if repairs were carried out by an unauthorised party. Normal cosmetic wear, scratches, dents and consumable items are excluded. The warranty does not cover loss or theft, software issues, virus removal, data recovery, or compatibility with third party software or peripherals. Display defects are assessed against a pixel policy that permits up to five bright sub-pixels and up to ten dark sub-pixels within the active area before the panel is deemed defective.

5. CLAIM PROCEDURE
A warranty claim requires the original invoice, the serial number from the base of the device, and a description of the fault. Claims may be lodged through the support portal, by telephone or at an authorised service centre. Diagnosis takes up to five working days after the device is received. Replacement with a refurbished equivalent unit may be made where repair is not economical or parts are unavailable; a new unit replacement is provided only within the first fifteen days of purchase. The repaired or replaced item carries the remainder of the original warranty period or ninety days from the date of return, whichever is longer.

6. CONSUMER GUARANTEES
Nothing in this warranty excludes, restricts or modifies any consumer guarantee, right or remedy conferred by applicable consumer law which cannot be excluded, restricted or modified by agreement. This warranty is additional to any statutory rights available to the consumer.
question: What is the warranty period for the Apexbook Pro 14 laptop itself, how long is the battery covered, and what specifically voids the warranty?
reference_answer: The laptop carries a limited hardware warranty of thirty six months from the date of original retail purchase, covering parts and labour at authorised service centres, with on-site service for the first twelve months. The battery is covered separately for twelve months or three hundred charge cycles, whichever comes first. The warranty is void if the serial number label is removed or altered, if the bottom panel seal is broken by an unauthorised person, or if repairs were carried out by an unauthorised party, and it also excludes accident, abuse, liquid contact and non-approved accessories.

title: Payment Gateway API Documentation
long_prompt:
MERIDIAN PAYMENTS DEVELOPER GUIDE - API VERSION 4.2
BASE URL: https://api.meridianpay.example/v4

1. AUTHENTICATION
All requests require a bearer token obtained through the OAuth 2.0 client credentials flow at the token endpoint. Tokens expire after 3600 seconds and must be refreshed by the client. Requests without a valid token return HTTP 401 with an error body of type invalid_client. Requests with a valid token but insufficient scope return HTTP 403 with an error body of type insufficient_scope. IP allowlisting is enforced on live mode keys; test mode keys have no allowlist restriction. Secret keys must never be exposed in client side code, mobile applications or public repositories. Rotation of a secret key invalidates the previous key immediately with no overlap period.

2. IDEMPOTENCY
Every creation request accepts an optional idempotency key header, which is a client generated string of up to 64 characters drawn from the set of alphanumeric characters, hyphen and underscore. Keys are retained for 24 hours from first use. If a request is received with an idempotency key that has already been used within the retention window, the server replays the stored response for the original request, including the original status code, and returns the header Idempotency-Replayed: true. If the same key is used with a different HTTP method, a different endpoint, or a request body whose payload hash differs from the original, the server returns HTTP 409 Conflict with an error body of type idempotency_key_conflict. Replayed responses return HTTP 200 OK rather than the status of the original creation, so clients must inspect the resource object rather than relying on the status code alone. Requests without an idempotency key are not protected against duplicate submission; clients must always send a key on payment creation to guard against network retries.

3. CORE ENDPOINTS
POST /charges creates a charge and returns 201 Created. GET /charges/{id} retrieves a charge and returns 200 OK. POST /refunds creates a full or partial refund. GET /balances returns the current balance. POST /payouts initiates a transfer to a linked bank account. All list endpoints support cursor based pagination with a default page size of 25 and a maximum of 100, using the query parameters limit and starting_after.

4. ERROR MODEL
Errors are returned as JSON with the fields error, type, code, message and param. Rate limiting returns HTTP 429 with the headers Retry-After, X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset. Server errors return HTTP 500 or 503 and must be retried with exponential backoff. Validation failures return HTTP 422 with a param specific message. Card declines return HTTP 402 with a decline code such as card_declined, insufficient_funds, expired_card or incorrect_cvc.

5. WEBHOOKS
Webhook endpoints must respond within 5 seconds with any 2xx status code; slow endpoints are retried with exponential backoff for up to 72 hours. Payloads are signed with HMAC SHA-256 using the endpoint secret and the header Meridian-Signature, formatted as t=1700000000,v1=<hex digest> over the string "{t}.{raw_body}". Consumers must verify the timestamp within a tolerance of 300 seconds to prevent replay attacks. Event types include charge.succeeded, charge.failed, refund.updated, payout.failed and balance.available.

6. RATE LIMITS
Live mode allows 100 requests per second per account. Test mode allows 25 requests per second. Bursts are smoothed with a token bucket of capacity equal to twice the per second rate. Exceeding the limit returns 429 and does not penalise the account, but sustained abuse may trigger temporary suspension pending review.

7. VERSIONING
Additive changes such as new fields or new endpoints are made without a version bump. Breaking changes such as removing a field, changing a type or changing an error code require a new major version. Version 4 is supported for 24 months after the release of version 5. Clients should read unknown fields defensively and must not crash on fields they do not recognise.

8. TEST MODE
Test mode uses the prefix sk_test_ and the sandbox host api.sandbox.meridianpay.example. Test cards exercise specific outcomes: 4000000000000002 always declines, 4000000000009995 returns insufficient funds, and 4000000000000069 returns an expired card. Test mode data is purged every ninety days.
question: What HTTP status code does the API return when an idempotency key is reused with a different request body, and how does a client detect that a response was replayed?
reference_answer: When the same idempotency key is reused with a different endpoint, method or request body, the server returns HTTP 409 Conflict with an error body of type idempotency_key_conflict. When a key is reused with the identical original request, the server replays the stored response with HTTP 200 OK and sets the response header Idempotency-Replayed to true, so the client detects a replay by checking that header and should inspect the resource object rather than relying on the status code.

title: University Examination and Promotion Regulations
long_prompt:
ALLIANCE UNIVERSITY - SCHOOL OF ENGINEERING
REGULATIONS FOR THE BACHELOR OF TECHNOLOGY PROGRAMME - R2023

1. CREDIT STRUCTURE
The programme requires a minimum of 160 credits for completion, distributed across university core courses, programme core courses, programme electives, a mandatory internship and a capstone project. Each theory course is normally worth 4 credits and each laboratory course 2 credits. A credit is earned when the student secures a cumulative grade point average of 5.0 or above in that course. Courses carrying fewer than 5.0 grade points must be repeated or replaced as per clause 4.

2. GRADE POINT SCALE
The grade point scale is: O equals 10, A equals 9, B equals 8, C equals 7, D equals 6, E equals 5 and F equals 0. A course graded F carries zero credits and must be repeated. The semester grade point average is the credit weighted mean of the grade points earned in that semester. The cumulative grade point average is the credit weighted mean across all semesters attempted.

3. ATTENDANCE REQUIREMENT
A student must secure a minimum of 75 percent attendance in each course as on the last working day of the semester to be permitted to write the end semester examination. A shortage of up to five percentage points may be condoned by the competent authority on medical or other genuine grounds, in which case the requirement becomes 70 percent. Detention for shortage of attendance is communicated in writing within one week of the publication of the timetable for the end semester examination.

4. PROMOTION FROM ONE SEMESTER TO THE NEXT
A student is promoted from the current semester to the next semester on satisfying all of the following conditions in a single attempt: securing a semester grade point average of 5.0 or above in the semester just completed; passing all courses of the immediately preceding semester; and having no more than two outstanding arrears in total across all earlier semesters at the time of promotion. A student who fails to satisfy these conditions is detained for one semester and must re-register only for the failed or deficient courses, paying the applicable retake examination fee. A student may be detained for a maximum of two semesters during the entire programme; a third failure to satisfy the promotion criteria results in removal from the programme.

5. ARREARS AND REPEAT LIMITATIONS
The total number of arrears carried at any point must not exceed four. If a student accumulates more than four arrears, promotion is withheld irrespective of the semester grade point average. Arrears in a laboratory course must be cleared within two subsequent offerings of that laboratory, otherwise the course must be taken afresh with the junior batch. Arrears cannot be cleared during a semester in which the student is on internship.

6. EXAMINATION AND ASSESSMENT
The end semester examination carries 60 marks and the internal assessment carries 40 marks. Internal assessment comprises two continuous assessments of 15 marks each and a laboratory or assignment component of 10 marks. A student securing an aggregate of less than 40 percent in a course, that is less than 40 marks out of 100, is deemed to have failed that course regardless of the internal marks already secured. Malpractice in any examination results in cancellation of the entire semester's results and disqualification from awards for a period of one year.

7. GRADE IMPROVEMENT
A student may apply for grade improvement in a maximum of two courses per semester, appearing for the improved examination in the next immediate offering. The improved grade, whether higher or lower, replaces the original grade. Grade improvement is not permitted in projects, internships or courses already cleared with an O grade.

8. CLASSIFICATION OF RESULTS
A student securing a cumulative grade point average of 7.5 or above with no arrears is declared a First Class with Distinction. A cumulative grade point average of 6.0 or above is declared First Class. A cumulative grade point average of 5.0 or above is declared Second Class. A student who completes all 160 credits with a cumulative grade point average below 5.0 is not awarded the degree.

9. CONDONATION
A shortage of up to two credits may be condoned by the Academic Council on the recommendation of the Board of Studies, provided the student has secured the minimum attendance in the condoned courses and has no arrears in the semester in which the condonation is sought.

10. REVALUATION
A student may apply for revaluation within seven days of publication of results by paying the prescribed fee per script. An increase of two or more marks triggers a third evaluation by an external examiner, and the third evaluation is final. Revaluation is not permitted for internal marks or laboratory assessments.
question: What semester grade point average and arrears conditions must a student satisfy to be promoted to the next semester?
reference_answer: To be promoted, a student must secure a semester grade point average of 5.0 or above in the semester just completed, pass all courses of the immediately preceding semester, and have no more than two outstanding arrears in total across all earlier semesters at the time of promotion, all in a single attempt. In addition, the total number of arrears carried at any point must not exceed four, otherwise promotion is withheld regardless of the semester grade point average.

title: Information Security and Access Control Policy
long_prompt:
MERIDIAN CORPORATE INFORMATION SECURITY POLICY
POLICY NUMBER SEC-AC-002 - VERSION 6.0 - REVIEW CYCLE ANNUAL
OWNER: CHIEF INFORMATION SECURITY OFFICER

1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE
This policy defines the requirements for authentication, access control, credential management and privileged access across all information systems owned or operated by the organisation. It applies to all employees, contractors, vendors, interns and third parties who access any corporate system, whether from company managed equipment, personal equipment or a mobile device. Non-compliance may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination of employment or contract, and may be referred to law enforcement where criminal conduct is suspected.

2. PASSWORD REQUIREMENTS
All user passwords must be a minimum of twelve characters in length and must contain characters from at least three of the following four classes: uppercase letters, lowercase letters, digits and special symbols. Passwords must not contain the user name, employee number or any substring of the user's display name longer than three characters. Passwords must not be reused from the last twelve generations of that user's password history. Passwords expire every ninety days, and users are notified at fourteen days, seven days, one day and one hour before expiry. A password may not be changed more than once in a four hour window, which prevents users from cycling rapidly through a sequence to return to a previous favourite password. Passwords must be stored only in the approved enterprise password manager and must never be written down, transmitted by email or chat, or stored in a plain text file, spreadsheet or source code repository.

3. ACCOUNT LOCKOUT AND THROTTLING
After five consecutive failed authentication attempts an account is locked for a period of fifteen minutes, after which it unlocks automatically. A sixth consecutive failure within the same window extends the lock to thirty minutes. Ten cumulative failures within a twenty four hour period trigger a mandatory lock requiring verification of identity at the service desk; automatic unlocking does not apply. Lockout events are written to the security event log and alert the security operations centre in real time when five or more accounts are locked within a ten minute window, which may indicate a credential stuffing attack. Administrators must never unlock an account without verifying the identity of the requester through the documented out of band process.

4. MULTI FACTOR AUTHENTICATION
Multi factor authentication is mandatory for all remote access, all cloud applications, all administrative access and all systems processing confidential data. Acceptable factors are hardware security keys supporting FIDO2 as the preferred option, authenticator applications supporting time based one time passwords, and push notifications to a registered managed device. SMS based second factors are prohibited except where no alternative exists and the risk has been accepted in writing by the Chief Information Security Officer. Multi factor authentication fatigue attacks, that is repeated push prompts, are mitigated by number matching and a maximum of three prompts before the request is blocked. Service accounts and machine identities are excluded from interactive multi factor authentication but must use certificate based authentication or a managed secret with automatic rotation not exceeding ninety days.

5. PRIVILEGED ACCESS MANAGEMENT
Privileged accounts are separate from standard accounts and must never be used for email, web browsing or ordinary productivity tasks. Administrative access is granted just in time through the privileged access management platform for a maximum session duration of eight hours, and standing privileged access is prohibited for all tiers except break glass accounts. Break glass accounts are sealed in the vault, their credentials are rotated after every use, and every use raises a priority one alert. All privileged sessions are recorded and retained for one year. Quarterly access recertification is performed by system owners; entitlements not confirmed within the recertification window are revoked automatically. Shared accounts are prohibited except for automated service identities where a shared identity is technically unavoidable, in which case the password must be rotated automatically every thirty days through the vault.

6. LEAVER AND MOVER PROCESS
Access is revoked within four hours of the effective termination date for voluntary exits and immediately for involuntary exits, as confirmed by the human resources termination feed which is synchronised hourly. Role changes trigger an entitlement review within two business days, and the previous role's access is removed at the time the new role's access is granted. Managers who do not complete the leaver checklist within the timeframe are escalated to their own manager.

7. MONITORING AND LOGGING
Authentication successes and failures, privilege escalations, permission changes and access denials are logged centrally and retained for twelve months online and twenty four months in archive. Logs are protected from modification by the account holder and are time synchronised to a common stratum two network time source. Alerting rules are reviewed monthly and tuned to reduce false positives.

8. EXCEPTIONS AND WAIVERS
Exceptions to this policy require a documented risk assessment, a compensating control, an expiry date not exceeding twelve months and approval by the Chief Information Security Officer. Exceptions are recorded in the risk register and reviewed at each quarterly security steering committee meeting.
question: How often must passwords be changed, what is the account lockout threshold, and how long does a lockout last?
reference_answer: Passwords expire every ninety days, with notifications at fourteen days, seven days, one day and one hour before expiry. An account is locked after five consecutive failed authentication attempts for fifteen minutes, and a sixth consecutive failure within the same window extends the lockout to thirty minutes. Ten cumulative failures within a twenty four hour period trigger a mandatory lock that does not auto-unlock and requires identity verification at the service desk.

title: E-commerce Return, Refund and Warranty Policy
long_prompt:
SHOPVERSE CUSTOMER RETURNS AND REFUNDS POLICY
LAST UPDATED: 12 DECEMBER 2024 - APPLICABLE TO ORDERS SHIPPED WITHIN INDIA

1. RETURN WINDOW BY CATEGORY
Electronics and appliances, whether new or used, may be returned within ten days of delivery. Fashion and apparel may be returned within fourteen days of delivery. Books, music and movies may be returned within seven days of delivery. Groceries, fresh produce, perishables, personal care items and anything sealed for hygiene reasons are non-returnable once delivered unless damaged, defective or incorrect on arrival. Furniture and large appliances larger than 40 kg may be returned within seven days of delivery and require a scheduled pick-up by our logistics partner. Gift cards, intimate wear, customised products and products assembled by the customer after delivery are non-returnable in all cases. The return window is calculated from the date of delivery as recorded in the proof of delivery, not the date of order placement or the date of payment.

2. CONDITION REQUIREMENTS
Returned items must be in their original condition with all tags, manual, accessories, free gifts, serial number stickers and original packaging intact. A product that has been used, installed, scratched, damaged or has missing parts may be refused at pick-up or at the quality check centre, in which case the item is shipped back to the customer at no charge. Opened software, activated subscription cards and redeemed vouchers cannot be returned. For electronics, the return is accepted provided the device has not been activated where activation is detectable, and the original invoice and box are presented.

3. HOW TO INITIATE A RETURN
A return is initiated from the order details page in the ShopVerse account or the mobile application within the applicable window. A reverse pick-up is scheduled within forty eight hours in most serviceable pin codes; where reverse pick-up is not available the customer may drop the item at a designated collection point or ship it themselves, with reimbursement of actual shipping cost against a valid receipt. Once the item reaches the quality check centre the inspection is completed within seventy two hours. If the item passes inspection the refund process begins immediately. If the item fails inspection the customer is informed by email and SMS with the specific reason and photographs of the finding.

4. REFUND METHOD AND TIMELINE
Refunds are credited to the original payment method used for the purchase. Payments made by credit card or debit card are refunded to the same card and typically reflect within five to seven working days depending on the issuing bank. Payments made by net banking are refunded to the source account within five working days. Payments made through a wallet are refunded to the same wallet within twenty four hours. Cash on delivery orders are refunded by electronic transfer to a bank account nominated by the customer, and the customer must provide bank details within thirty days of the return being approved, after which the claim expires. Promotional discounts and coupon values applied to the order are adjusted proportionally, so the refund amount may be lower than the price actually paid if part of the order is retained. Convenience fees, installation charges and express delivery charges are not refundable except where the order was incorrect or defective.

5. EXCHANGE
An exchange for a different size or colour is treated as a return plus a new order. Stock availability is not guaranteed and is confirmed only at the time the exchange order is created. Where the replacement item costs more the difference is collected through a payment link valid for twenty four hours; where it costs less the difference is refunded to the original payment method. One exchange is permitted per returned item.

6. DAMAGED, DEFECTIVE OR INCORRECT ITEMS
Items received damaged, defective or different from what was ordered may be returned within ten days of delivery irrespective of category, and the full refund including original shipping charges is processed. Manufacturing defects within the brand warranty period are handled by the brand's authorised service centre, and ShopVerse assists with routing the claim but is not the warranty provider. A refund for an incorrect or damaged item is processed within three working days of the quality check passing.

7. LATE PICK-UP AND FAILED PICK-UP
Where reverse pick-up fails twice for reasons attributable to the logistics partner, the customer may retain the item and the return is closed without refund. Where pick-up fails twice for reasons attributable to the customer, for example an incorrect address or unavailability, the return window lapses and the request is closed.

8. ABUSE AND FRAUD CONTROL
Accounts showing patterns of serial returns, empty box returns, switch returns or returns of counterfeit items are investigated and may have return privileges suspended for twelve months. Orders flagged by the fraud prevention system may be held for additional verification before dispatch. Abuse of the returns policy may result in termination of the account without prior notice.

9. STATUTORY RIGHTS
This policy is in addition to and does not limit any statutory right available to the consumer under applicable consumer protection law, including the right to a replacement or repair of goods that are defective at the time of delivery.
question: Within how many days can an electronic item be returned, and how is the refund issued for a credit card payment?
reference_answer: Electronics and appliances, whether new or used, may be returned within ten days of delivery, calculated from the delivery date recorded in the proof of delivery. The refund is credited to the original payment method, so for a credit card payment it is refunded to the same card and typically reflects within five to seven working days depending on the issuing bank. The item must be in original condition with tags, accessories and packaging intact, and promotional discounts are adjusted proportionally.

title: Paediatric Oral Antibiotic Dosing Protocol
long_prompt:
RIVERSIDE CHILDREN'S HOSPITAL - PAEDIATRIC ANTIMICROBIAL DOSING PROTOCOL
PROTOCOL ID PAP-AMR-2024-03 - EFFECTIVE 01 APRIL 2024
APPROVED BY: ANTI-MICROBIAL STEERING COMMITTEE

1. SCOPE AND SAFETY OVERVIEW
This protocol applies to inpatients and outpatients under eighteen years of age treated at Riverside Children's Hospital and its affiliated clinics. All doses must be verified against the patient's current weight, age, renal function and hepatic function before administration. Doses stated in this document are single doses for otherwise healthy children with normal renal and hepatic function. Where a dose range is given, the lower end is used for the first seventy two hours of therapy in children with impaired renal function. Weight based dosing always takes precedence over age based dosing when the two disagree, and the most recent documented weight in kilograms, measured within the preceding seventy two hours, must be used. Every dose must be independently double checked by a second registered nurse before administration, and the double check must be recorded in the electronic medication administration record.

2. AMOXICILLIN
Amoxicillin is dosed at 25 to 50 milligrams per kilogram of body weight per day divided into two doses for mild upper respiratory infection, and at 80 to 90 milligrams per kilogram of body weight per day divided into two to three doses for suspected bacterial meningitis or severe otitis media, not exceeding a maximum of 3 grams per day in any child over twelve months. The oral suspension is available in 125 milligrams per 5 millilitres, 250 milligrams per 5 millilitres and 400 milligrams per 5 millilitres strengths. The higher strength suspension is preferred for children above twenty kilograms to reduce the volume per dose and improve adherence. Reconstituted suspension must be stored at two to eight degrees Celsius and discarded after fourteen days.

3. AMOXICILLIN-CLAVULANATE
Amoxicillin-clavulanate is dosed at 45 to 90 milligrams per kilogram of body weight per day of the amoxicillin component divided into two doses, with a maximum amoxicillin component of 3 grams per day. The 7:1 ratio formulation is preferred where available because it permits higher amoxicillin dosing with less clavulanate and therefore less diarrhoea. Where only the 4:1 formulation is available the dose must not exceed 45 milligrams per kilogram per day to avoid clavulanate-related gastrointestinal intolerance. Administration must be with food to reduce gastric irritation.

4. CEFPODOXIME
Cefpodoxime is dosed at 5 milligrams per kilogram of body weight every twelve hours for upper respiratory infection and at 10 milligrams per kilogram of body weight every twelve hours for lower respiratory tract infection, with a maximum of 400 milligrams per day. The suspension must not be given with milk or antacids as absorption is reduced by approximately thirty percent. In renal impairment with a creatinine clearance below 30 millilitres per minute per 1.73 square metres the interval is extended to twenty four hours.

5. AZITHROMYCIN
Azithromycin is dosed at 10 milligrams per kilogram on day one followed by 5 milligrams per kilogram once daily on days two to five, with a maximum total course dose of 30 milligrams per kilogram or 1.5 grams whichever is lower. Azithromycin is not to be used empirically where the local resistance rate for the suspected organism exceeds twenty percent, and must be checked against the hospital antibiogram before prescribing. It is contraindicated in children with a known prolongation of the QT interval or on other QT-prolonging medication.

6. DOSING BANDS FOR COMMON WEIGHTS
For a child weighing ten kilograms the single dose of amoxicillin at 25 to 50 milligrams per kilogram is 250 to 500 milligrams per day divided into two doses, that is 125 to 250 milligrams per dose. For a child weighing fifteen kilograms the corresponding daily dose is 375 to 750 milligrams. For a child weighing twenty kilograms the daily dose at the standard range is 500 to 1000 milligrams, that is 250 to 500 milligrams per dose twice daily; at the meningitis range of 80 to 90 milligrams per kilogram the daily dose is 1600 to 1800 milligrams divided into two or three doses, not exceeding the 3 gram ceiling. For a child weighing thirty kilograms the standard range daily dose is 750 to 1500 milligrams, and the dose is capped by adult dosing once the calculated dose exceeds the adult maximum. Doses above the adult maximum must never be administered to a child regardless of weight.

7. RENAL ADJUSTMENT
For amoxicillin, when the creatinine clearance is 10 to 30 millilitres per minute per 1.73 square metres, the interval is extended to twelve hours. Below 10 millilitres per minute per 1.73 square metres a single daily dose at twenty five percent of the normal total is given. Neonates under one month of age have immature renal function and must be dosed at twenty five percent of the standard paediatric dose at intervals of twelve to twenty four hours with therapeutic drug monitoring.

8. DOCUMENTATION AND MONITORING
The dose, weight, time, route and the two-nurse verification are recorded in the electronic medication administration record at the time of administration, not retrospectively. Culture results and clinical response are reviewed at forty eight hours, and any change in therapy is documented with a note explaining the rationale. Adverse drug reactions are reported to the hospital pharmacovigilance officer within twenty four hours of identification.

9. EXCLUSIONS
This protocol does not cover intravenous loading doses, extended infusion regimens, therapeutic drug monitoring targets, or dosing in patients on continuous renal replacement therapy, for which the separate protocol PAP-AMR-2024-07 must be consulted.
question: What is the recommended single dose range of amoxicillin for a child weighing twenty kilograms at the standard range and at the meningitis range?
reference_answer: For a twenty kilogram child, at the standard range of 25 to 50 milligrams per kilogram per day the daily dose is 500 to 1000 milligrams, giving 250 to 500 milligrams per dose twice daily. At the meningitis range of 80 to 90 milligrams per kilogram per day the daily dose is 1600 to 1800 milligrams divided into two or three doses, and it must not exceed the maximum of 3 grams per day.

title: Commercial Kitchen Food Safety Manual
long_prompt:
THE HARBOUR KITCHEN - FOOD SAFETY AND HYGIENE MANUAL
MANUAL REFERENCE HK-FSM-11 - ISSUE 4
APPLICABLE TO: ALL FOOD HANDLING STAFF, SUPERVISORS AND MANAGEMENT

1. TEMPERATURE CONTROL
Ready to eat food that requires temperature control must be held at or below 5 degrees Celsius or at or above 63 degrees Celsius at all times. The danger zone between 5 and 63 degrees Celsius must be traversed as rapidly as possible and in no case may food remain in the danger zone for more than two hours in total across all handling, transport and preparation steps. Chilled display units must be set to operate at 3 degrees Celsius with an alarm configured to trigger at 5 degrees Celsius. Frozen storage must be maintained at minus 18 degrees Celsius or below. Hot holding units must maintain food at 63 degrees Celsius or above, and food held in hot holding for more than four hours must be discarded and must not be re-heated or re-used in any dish.

2. TEMPERATURE CHECKING AND RECORDS
Refrigerators and freezers are checked and recorded twice per shift, at the start of the morning shift and at the start of the evening shift, with an additional check at the close of service every day. Every temperature probe is calibrated before each shift using the ice water method, which must read 0 degrees Celsius plus or minus 0.5 degrees Celsius, or using a certified reference solution. Probes that fail calibration are removed from service and tagged. Calibration and temperature records are retained for a minimum of ninety days and are available for inspection at any time by the local authority. Any reading outside the permitted range triggers an immediate corrective action which is recorded with the action taken, the time, and the name of the person taking the action.

3. COOKING AND REHEATING TEMPERATURES
Poultry, minced meat products and mechanically tenderised meat must reach a core temperature of 74 degrees Celsius held for fifteen seconds. Whole cuts of red meat must reach 63 degrees Celsius for fifteen seconds with a permissible pink centre only for whole cuts, never for minced or tenderised product. Leftover food intended for re-service must be cooled from 63 degrees Celsius to 21 degrees Celsius within two hours and from 21 degrees Celsius to 5 degrees Celsius within a further four hours, for a total cooling time of no more than six hours. Cooling is achieved using shallow trays no deeper than 50 millimetres, ice wands, or a blast chiller; a blast chiller must bring food from 63 degrees Celsius to 5 degrees Celsius within ninety minutes. Reheating must reach 74 degrees Celsius within two hours and food may be re-heated only once.

4. PERSONAL HYGIENE
All food handlers must hold a current food handler certificate, valid for three years, and must renew it before expiry. Hands must be washed with soap and warm water for at least twenty seconds on entering the preparation area, after handling raw protein, after using the toilet, after touching the face or hair, after handling waste, and after any activity that contaminates the hands. Hand sanitiser is a supplement to, and never a substitute for, hand washing. Single use gloves must be changed between tasks and whenever torn or contaminated. Cuts and wounds must be covered with a blue detectable plaster and a waterproof finger cot, and a food handler with a diarrhoeal or vomiting illness must not work in food handling for at least forty eight hours after symptoms cease. Fingernails must be short and unvarnished, jewellery limited to a plain wedding band, and hair must be fully restrained by a hat or hairnet.

5. ALLERGEN MANAGEMENT
The fourteen declarable allergens are cereals containing gluten, crustaceans, eggs, fish, peanuts, soybeans, milk, nuts, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphur dioxide and sulphites, lupin and molluscs. Each dish has a documented allergen matrix which is updated whenever a recipe changes and is re-verified quarterly. Allergen information must be available to front of house staff in both printed and digital form at the point of service. A separate preparation area, colour coded boards, colour coded utensils and dedicated fryers are used for allergen-free orders. Where an allergen-free meal is ordered, the supervisor on duty must personally verify the plate before it leaves the kitchen. Cross contamination between raw and ready to eat food is prevented by colour coded chopping boards: red for raw meat, blue for raw fish, green for fruit and salad, yellow for cooked meat, brown for vegetables and white for dairy and bread.

6. CLEANING AND SANITATION
Food contact surfaces are cleaned and sanitised before each use and at least every four hours during continuous service. Cleaning chemicals are stored separately from food and food packaging, are never decanted into food containers, and are used only at the dilution stated on the dilution chart posted at each chemical station. Colour coded cloths are used per zone and laundered daily at sixty degrees Celsius. A master cleaning schedule lists every item of equipment, the frequency, the chemical, the method and the person responsible, and is signed off by the shift supervisor daily.

7. PEST CONTROL AND WASTE
Pest control is carried out by a licensed contractor on a monthly schedule with reports retained for two years. All external doors must be fitted with self closing devices and air curtains in operation. Waste is removed from the preparation area at least every two hours, bins are kept closed, and waste is stored in a locked external compound for collection three times per week.

8. RECEIVING AND STORAGE OF GOODS
Deliveries are rejected if chilled goods exceed 8 degrees Celsius, frozen goods show signs of thawing, or packaging is damaged or contaminated. Receiving checks are recorded on the goods inwards log with the delivery time, temperature, condition and the name of the receiver. Stock is rotated on a first in first out basis with date labels showing the date of preparation, the use by date and the initials of the person preparing it. Dry goods are stored at least 150 millimetres above the floor and 500 millimetres away from walls.

9. RECORDS AND TRAINING
All training records, temperature logs, calibration records, cleaning schedules, pest control reports and supplier approval records are retained for ninety days minimum and for twelve months for supplier and allergen documentation. Refresher training is delivered quarterly to all food handlers and training is repeated in full whenever this manual is re-issued.
question: At what temperature must chilled food be stored and held, and how often must refrigerator temperatures be checked and recorded?
reference_answer: Chilled food must be stored and held at or below 5 degrees Celsius, with chilled display units set to operate at 3 degrees Celsius and an alarm that triggers at 5 degrees Celsius. Refrigerator and freezer temperatures must be checked and recorded twice per shift, once at the start of the morning shift and once at the start of the evening shift, with an additional check at the close of service every day, and every probe must be calibrated before each shift by the ice water method.

title: Motor Insurance Policy - Own Damage and Depreciation
long_prompt:
SECURECARE GENERAL INSURANCE LIMITED
MOTOR PACKAGE POLICY - PRIVATE CAR - SCHEDULE AND WORDING
POLICY TYPE: STANDALONE OWN DAMAGE WITH THIRD PARTY LIABILITY

1. DEFINITIONS
The insured declared value, abbreviated IDV, is the sum insured fixed for the vehicle and is deemed to be the present market value of the vehicle. Market value is determined as the manufacturer's listed selling price less depreciation as per the age based schedule in clause 4, less the cost of registration and taxes if separately shown. The IDV for accessories not included in the manufacturer's list is fixed separately at an amount agreed in writing and is subject to a maximum of one percent of the IDV for standard fittings.

2. SCOPE OF COVER
This policy covers loss of or damage to the insured vehicle caused by accident, theft, fire, explosion, self ignition, lightning, earthquake, flood, inundation, hailstorm, frost, cyclone, typhoon, tempest, storm, hurricane and similar perils, rockslide, landslide, accidental external means, malicious acts, riot and strike, terrorism as an optional extension, and whilst in transit by road, rail, inland waterway, lift, elevator or air. The policy also covers damages caused to third parties including bodily injury, death and property damage up to the statutory limits applicable under the Motor Vehicles Act as amended from time to time.

3. EXCLUSIONS
The policy does not cover loss or damage due to wear and tear, gradual deterioration, mechanical or electrical breakdown, overloading or misriage, depreciation, consequential loss, or damage caused whilst the vehicle is being driven by a person who does not hold a valid driving licence or is under the influence of alcohol or drugs. Loss of or damage to tyres unless caused by an accident at the same time as damage to the vehicle is excluded, save that the policy pays fifty percent of the cost of replacement of tyres if the tyres are damaged in an accident in which the vehicle also suffers damage. Damage to the vehicle whilst being used for hire or reward, racing, pace making, or whilst in breach of any warranty of use is excluded. The policy does not cover claims arising out of war, invasion, act of foreign enemy, nuclear perils, or contractual liability.

4. DEPRECIATION SCHEDULE FOR OWN DAMAGE CLAIMS
Depreciation is applied to the age of the vehicle calculated from the date of registration to the date of loss. Rubber, nylon and plastic parts, battery and tyres are depreciated at fifty percent. Fibre glass components are depreciated at thirty percent. All other parts are depreciated according to the following schedule: vehicle of age not exceeding six months is depreciated at five percent; over six months but not exceeding one year, fifteen percent; over one year but not exceeding two years, twenty percent; over two years but not exceeding three years, thirty percent; over three years but not exceeding four years, forty percent; over four years but not exceeding five years, fifty percent; over five years but not exceeding ten years, sixty percent; and over ten years, seventy percent. Glass parts are depreciated at nil. The schedule is applied to the claim settlement amount and not to the IDV itself when computing a total loss.

5. TOTAL LOSS AND CONSTRUCTIVE TOTAL LOSS
A claim is settled as a total loss where the cost of repair exceeds seventy five percent of the IDV immediately before the loss, or where the vehicle is declared a total loss by the insurer after theft, or where the vehicle is not recovered within one hundred and eighty days of the theft being reported. In a total loss settlement the depreciated IDV is payable less the salvage value determined by the insurer, and ownership of the vehicle vests in the insurer upon payment. A constructive total loss declaration requires a surveyor's estimate and the approval of the branch claims manager.

6. DEDUCTIBLES AND VOLUNTARY EXCESS
A compulsory excess of one thousand rupees is applicable to every claim under the own damage section. A voluntary excess chosen by the insured at inception is applied in addition to the compulsory excess and reduces the premium. Where the insured has opted for a voluntary excess of two thousand five hundred rupees the total excess payable per claim is three thousand five hundred rupees. Excess is not applicable to third party liability claims.

7. NO CLAIM BONUS
A no claim bonus of twenty percent for the first claim free year, twenty five percent for the second, thirty five percent for the third, forty five percent for the fourth and fifty percent for the fifth and subsequent years is available on renewal. The maximum aggregate no claim bonus is fifty percent. The no claim bonus is reduced or forfeited upon the lodging of a claim, and restoration of the full bonus is subject to the insurer's reinstatement rules. Bonus earned with one insurer is transferable on production of a letter of experience.

8. CLAIM PROCEDURE
Intimate the claim to the call centre within forty eight hours of discovery or the nearest branch office. Obtain a police report in cases of theft, third party injury or hit and run. Complete the claim form and submit it with the driving licence, registration certificate, insurance policy, repair estimate and any medical documents within thirty days of the incident. The vehicle must not be repaired before the surveyor's inspection and written authorisation, except in an emergency where life or property is at risk, in which case evidence of the emergency must be produced. Settlement is made by reimbursement against original invoices or by cashless settlement at a network workshop. Claims are ordinarily settled within thirty days of submission of all necessary documents, and delay beyond thirty days attracts interest at the rate prescribed by the insurance regulator.

9. CONSUMER DUTIES
The insured must take all reasonable steps to avert or minimise loss, must not abandon the vehicle without the insurer's consent, must give all information required, and must not admit liability or make any offer or promise of settlement without the insurer's written approval. Any fraud, misrepresentation or non-disclosure renders the claim voidable and the policy liable to be cancelled from inception with refund of premium limited to unearned proportion.
question: What depreciation rate is applied to a vehicle between three and four years old under the own damage schedule, and what is the compulsory excess on every own damage claim?
reference_answer: A vehicle over three years but not exceeding four years of age is depreciated at forty percent under the own damage schedule. A compulsory excess of one thousand rupees applies to every claim under the own damage section, to which any voluntary excess chosen at inception is added; the excess does not apply to third party liability claims. Rubber, nylon, plastic, battery and tyres are separately depreciated at fifty percent, glass at nil.

title: Library v4 Release Notes and Migration Guide
long_prompt:
NOVAJSON - RELEASE NOTES AND MIGRATION GUIDE
LATEST RELEASE: VERSION 4.0.0 - RELEASE DATE 15 JANUARY 2025

1. HIGHLIGHTS OF VERSION 4
NovaJSON 4 is a major release that reworks the parsing core, changes the default behaviour of the parser in three breaking ways, and drops support for end of life runtimes. The release reduces median parse time by approximately forty percent on typical payloads and reduces peak memory usage by roughly twenty five percent through a zero-copy string handling path. It introduces first class support for streaming parsing of JSON Lines, a pluggable number format handler, and a stable TypeScript type generation command.

2. BREAKING CHANGES
2.1 Duplicate keys are now rejected by default. In version 3 the last occurrence of a duplicate key silently won. In version 4 the parser raises a DuplicateKeyError at the position of the second occurrence. The legacy behaviour is available only by setting the option allowDuplicateKeys to true, which is not recommended because it masks upstream data bugs. This is the single most common cause of upgrade failures and must be handled before upgrading.

2.2 Trailing commas are now rejected by default. Version 3 accepted a trailing comma in objects and arrays. Version 4 raises a TrailingCommaError. The option allowTrailingCommas exists but is deprecated and will be removed in version 5.

2.3 The default maximum nesting depth has been reduced from 512 to 64. Deeply nested payloads such as generated AST dumps will raise a DepthExceededError. Raise the limit explicitly with maxDepth if the reduction affects your workload, and consider whether such deeply nested input is really required.

2.4 Runtime support: Node.js 16 and Python 3.7 have been dropped. The minimum supported versions are Node.js 18, Python 3.9, .NET 6 and Java 11. Attempting to install on an unsupported runtime fails with a clear engine error rather than producing undefined behaviour.

2.5 The named export parseAsync has been removed in favour of parse with the streaming option enabled. parseAsync remains as a deprecated alias that emits a warning in 4.x and will be removed in 5.0.

2.6 Error objects no longer carry the deprecated err.value property; use err.partialResult instead, which is populated even when parsing fails so that recovery logic can inspect how far the parser progressed.

3. MIGRATION STEPS
Step 1: upgrade to the latest 3.x release, which is 3.9.4, and run your test suite. Step 2: fix every deprecation warning emitted by 3.9.4, in particular parseAsync and err.value. Step 3: upgrade to 4.0.0. Step 4: address DuplicateKeyError failures by fixing the data producer or, only if the duplication is legitimate and order independent, by setting allowDuplicateKeys to true as a temporary measure. Step 5: review any payload with more than 64 levels of nesting and raise maxDepth only where the structure is genuinely required. Step 6: run the bundled codemod with the command npx novajson-codemod migrate --from 3 --to 4 ./src, which rewrites parseAsync call sites and replaces err.value with err.partialResult automatically. Step 7: update your continuous integration matrix to the supported runtimes.

4. NEW FEATURES
4.1 Streaming JSON Lines: the new parseStream async generator accepts an async iterable of chunks and yields one parsed value per line without buffering the whole input. It handles partial chunks that split a value across chunk boundaries and exposes a backpressure signal through the returned controller.

4.2 Pluggable number formats: a numberFormat hook lets you decode big integers as BigInt, decode decimal strings exactly, or reject all numbers outside a given range. The default remains IEEE 754 double for backward compatibility.

4.3 Type generation: the command novajson generate-types --schema schema.json --out types.ts produces a discriminated union type from a JSON schema. The generated file is deterministic and safe to commit.

4.4 Improved error messages: errors now include a code frame showing the offending line with a caret at the failing column, plus a machine readable error code suitable for matching in tests.

5. PERFORMANCE
Benchmarks on a 10 MB synthetic document show parse time falling from 168 milliseconds in 3.9.4 to 101 milliseconds in 4.0.0 on Node.js 20, and peak heap falling from 96 MB to 72 MB. Performance characteristics degrade linearly with document size and are unchanged for documents below 100 KB. The streaming parser sustains approximately 220 MB per second on the same hardware.

6. SECURITY
Version 4 patches a prototype pollution vector in the schema validator, assigned CVE-2024-8841, which affected only the optional schema validation module and not the core parser. All users of the schema validator are advised to upgrade immediately. Version 4 also removes the dependency on the legacy buffer polyfill.

7. DEPRECATIONS AND THE ROAD TO VERSION 5
allowTrailingCommas, parseAsync and err.value are deprecated in 4.x and will be removed in 5.0. The legacy default export is replaced by named exports; importing the default export still works in 4.x with a warning. The maintainers recommend adopting named imports now to avoid a second migration later.

8. SUPPORT
Version 3 receives critical security fixes until 30 June 2025 and receives no feature work after the release of 4.0.0. Questions about migration should be raised on the community forum under the tag upgrade-v4, and confirmed bugs should be filed with a minimal reproduction.
question: What is the breaking change regarding duplicate keys in version 4, and what is the recommended migration step to handle it?
reference_answer: In version 4 duplicate keys are rejected by default, raising a DuplicateKeyError at the position of the second occurrence, whereas in version 3 the last occurrence of a duplicate key silently won. The recommended migration step is to fix the data producer that emits the duplicate keys; only where the duplication is legitimate and order independent should the option allowDuplicateKeys be set to true, and only as a temporary measure.

title: Metropolitan Transit Fares and Penalty Rules
long_prompt:
METROPOLITAN TRANSIT AUTHORITY - FARES, VALIDATION AND ENFORCEMENT RULES
RULE BOOK MTAR-2025 - APPLIES TO ALL RAIL, BUS AND TRAM SERVICES IN THE METROPOLITAN AREA

1. FARE STRUCTURE
Fares are zoned based. The metropolitan area is divided into nine zones, zone one being the central business district and zone nine the outermost suburban boundary. A single journey ticket is priced by the number of zones crossed. A journey wholly within one zone costs 1.50. Two zones cost 2.40. Three zones cost 3.20. Four zones cost 4.10. Five zones cost 5.00. Six zones cost 6.00. Seven zones cost 7.10. Eight zones cost 8.30. All nine zones cost 9.60. Child fares for children aged five to fifteen inclusive are charged at fifty percent of the adult single fare, and children under five travel free when accompanied by a fare paying passenger. Senior citizens aged sixty five and over and holders of a recognised concessionary pass travel free at all times on off peak services and at a fifty percent discount on peak services. Full time students holding a validated student concession card pay at seventy percent of the adult fare.

2. VALIDATION AND ZONE TRANSFER
A ticket or smartcard must be validated at the barrier or on board before boarding, and re-validated when changing between services where the transfer crosses a zone boundary. A transfer within the same zone on a through ticket is free for ninety minutes from the first validation. A journey interrupted for longer than ninety minutes is treated as a new journey. Passing through a barrier without validation, or re-using an already validated contactless card within the ninety minute window for a different origin-destination pair, is treated as travelling without a valid ticket. Season tickets and stored value cards must carry a minimum balance at the moment of validation; a zero balance at validation is treated as no ticket.

3. PENALTIES FOR TRAVELLING WITHOUT A VALID TICKET
A passenger found travelling without a valid ticket is liable to a penalty fare of the maximum single fare for the journey concerned plus a penalty of fifty pounds, giving a total that cannot be less than eighty pounds for any single offence. Where the passenger is a repeat offender, defined as a second or subsequent offence within twelve months, the penalty is doubled to one hundred pounds plus the maximum single fare, and the second offence is recorded against the passenger's concession account. Where the passenger holds a concessionary or student pass, the pass may be confiscated for a period of six months for a first offence and cancelled permanently for a second offence within twelve months. Payment of a penalty fare does not entitle the passenger to travel for the remainder of the day.

4. PENALTY FARE PROCESS
Penalty fare notices are issued at the time of inspection or posted within fourteen days of detection. Payment is due within twenty one days of the date of the notice. Payment within fourteen days attracts a discount of fifty percent, reducing the standard penalty of fifty pounds to twenty five pounds plus the maximum single fare. An appeal may be lodged within twenty eight days of the notice date on the grounds of a valid ticket having been held, a barrier fault, misleading signage, an incomplete journey caused by a service disruption, or exceptional personal circumstances. Appeals are determined within twenty one days and the outcome is notified in writing. Where an appeal is lodged the enforcement action is suspended pending determination, and the passenger must still travel with a valid ticket in the meantime. Failure to pay within the due date results in a recovery notice with an additional administration charge of thirty pounds; failure to pay that notice permits commencement of civil proceedings for the debt plus reasonable costs.

5. INSPECTION AND POWERS
Authorised revenue protection officers may inspect any ticket, pass or concession card at any time and may require a passenger to produce proof of identity. Passengers must not obstruct, delay or refuse an inspection; obstructing an inspection is an offence and may result in a penalty of two hundred pounds in addition to the fare penalty. Officers do not have the power to detain a passenger, but may retain a ticket or pass pending investigation and must issue a receipt for anything retained. Covert enforcement operations are carried out in accordance with the authority's approved code of practice.

6. REFUNDS AND DISRUPTION
A delay of fifteen minutes or more on rail, or thirty minutes or more on bus, entitles the holder of an anytime ticket to a delay repay of twenty five percent of the single fare for a delay of fifteen to twenty nine minutes, fifty percent for thirty to fifty nine minutes, and one hundred percent for sixty minutes or more. Season ticket holders claim delay repay on a pro rata basis against the season fare. Tickets are not refundable once validated unless the journey was not commenced, in which case an unused ticket may be returned within seven days for a full refund less a processing charge of one pound.

7. CONCESSIONARY PASS CONDITIONS
A concessionary pass is personal to the holder and is not transferable. Lending a pass to another person invalidates the pass and may result in cancellation together with a penalty of one hundred pounds. The pass must be produced on demand together with photographic identification. Lost passes are replaced once without charge and subsequently at a charge of fifteen pounds. A replacement pass takes up to five working days to issue, during which a temporary travel authority may be granted at the ticket office.

8. CONTACTLESS AND ACCOUNT BASED TAPPING
Contactless bank cards are charged the daily cap for the zones travelled in any calendar day, so a passenger making several journeys never pays more than the price of a daily ticket for the zones used. The daily cap is calculated overnight and the weekly cap is calculated from Monday to Sunday. Contactless cards issued outside the country of the authority's payment scheme may not be charged the cap automatically and the passenger is responsible for claiming the difference.

9. REVIEW
This rule book is reviewed annually by the Revenue Protection Committee and any change to penalty levels takes effect only after being published for a minimum of twenty eight days and displayed at all stations and on the authority website.
question: What penalty does a passenger pay for travelling without a valid ticket, how is it calculated, and what discount applies for early payment?
reference_answer: A passenger found travelling without a valid ticket is liable to the maximum single fare for the journey plus a penalty of fifty pounds, with a total that cannot be less than eighty pounds for a first offence. For a repeat offence within twelve months the penalty doubles to one hundred pounds plus the maximum single fare, and concessionary or student passes may be confiscated for six months or cancelled. Payment within fourteen days of the notice date attracts a fifty percent discount, reducing the fifty pound penalty to twenty five pounds plus the maximum single fare; payment is otherwise due within twenty one days.

title: Logistics Service Level Agreement
long_prompt:
VELOCITY LOGISTICS - SERVICE LEVEL AGREEMENT
SLA REFERENCE VL-SLA-2025-071
BETWEEN VELOCITY LOGISTICS PRIVATE LIMITED (THE PROVIDER) AND THE CLIENT NAMED IN THE SCHEDULE
EFFECTIVE FROM THE FIRST DAY OF THE MONTH FOLLOWING EXECUTION - TERM TWELVE MONTHS, RENEWING AUTOMATICALLY

1. SERVICES
The Provider shall receive, store, pick, pack and dispatch goods from the distribution centre named in the schedule. The services comprise inbound receiving and put away, inventory storage, order picking and packing, outbound dispatch, returns processing, inventory reporting and value added services such as kitting and labelling. The Provider shall perform the services with the skill and care reasonably expected of a competent logistics operator and shall maintain the warehouse management system in a state of continuous availability except during agreed maintenance windows.

2. SERVICE LEVEL METRICS AND TARGETS
2.1 Inbound receiving: ninety eight percent of pallets received and put away within eight working hours of the vehicle arriving at the dock. A working hour means an hour within the agreed operating window of 06:00 to 22:00 local time, excluding public holidays.
2.2 Order picking accuracy: ninety nine point five percent of order lines picked without error, measured monthly as one minus the number of incorrect lines divided by total lines picked.
2.3 Dispatch on time: ninety nine percent of orders picked, packed and handed to the carrier before the carrier cut off time for the relevant service level, where the cut off is 16:00 for next day service and 14:00 for same day service.
2.4 Inventory record accuracy: ninety nine point eight percent of cycle count locations matching the system record, measured on a rolling three month basis with a minimum of two thousand locations counted per quarter.
2.5 Returns processing: ninety five percent of returned items inspected, graded and dispositioned within forty eight hours of receipt at the returns dock.
2.6 Carrier collection failures: no more than zero point five percent of scheduled carrier collections missed per month.
2.7 System availability: ninety nine point five percent monthly availability of the warehouse management system and the client facing portal, excluding agreed maintenance windows of four hours per calendar month scheduled with at least five business days notice.

3. MEASUREMENT AND REPORTING
Performance is measured from the Provider's warehouse management system data which is exported to the Client monthly within five business days of month end, together with a dashboard showing the trend for each metric over the preceding twelve months. Where the Client disputes a measurement it must notify the Provider within ten business days of the monthly report, failing which the measurement is deemed accepted. The parties shall meet quarterly to review performance, open corrective actions and agree improvement plans. Measurement disputes that cannot be resolved at the operational level are escalated to the designated account managers within five business days.

4. SERVICE CREDITS
Where a metric is missed in a calendar month the Client is entitled to a service credit calculated as follows. For each full percentage point below target on order picking accuracy or dispatch on time, a credit of one percent of that month's storage and handling charges applies, capped in aggregate at ten percent of those charges in any one month. If picking accuracy falls below ninety seven percent or dispatch on time falls below ninety five percent in any single month, or if either metric misses target in three consecutive months, the Client may terminate the agreement immediately on written notice without penalty. For inventory record accuracy below ninety nine percent the credit is two percent of monthly storage charges per percentage point below target. Missed carrier collection attracts a flat credit of two hundred and fifty rupees per missed scheduled collection. System availability below ninety nine percent attracts a credit of five percent of the monthly platform fee per full point below target. Service credits are the Client's sole financial remedy for a failure to meet a service level, save for the termination right in clause 4 and the limitations in clause 8. Credits are applied against the invoice for the following month.

5. CAPACITY AND VOLUME COMMITMENT
The Client commits to a minimum monthly volume of twelve thousand order lines and a maximum of twenty five thousand order lines at the agreed rate card. Volumes above the maximum require thirty days written notice and are charged at the rates in the overage schedule, being one hundred and twenty percent of the base rate for volumes up to one hundred and twenty percent of the maximum and one hundred and fifty percent beyond that. The Provider shall maintain sufficient labour and equipment to handle the committed volume plus twenty percent surge capacity during the period from the first of November to the fifteenth of January. Failure to provide committed surge capacity is a material breach.

6. INVENTORY LOSS AND DAMAGE
The Provider is liable for shortage or damage to goods in its custody save where the loss arises from acts of God, inherent vice of the goods, acts of government, war, civil commotion, strikes or the negligence of the Client or its carriers. Liability for shortage or damage is limited to the replacement cost of the affected goods up to a maximum of five hundred thousand rupees per occurrence and one million rupees in aggregate in any contract year, unless the parties have agreed a higher declared value in the schedule. Claims must be notified within thirty days of the Client becoming aware of the loss and must be supported by documentary evidence of value. The Provider shall maintain warehouse all risk insurance for not less than the declared value of the goods held at any time and shall name the Client as an interested party.

7. DATA PROTECTION AND CONFIDENTIALITY
Each party shall comply with applicable data protection law. The Provider shall process personal data contained in order records only on the documented instructions of the Client, shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures, and shall notify the Client of any personal data breach without undue delay and in any event within seventy two hours of becoming aware. Order data, pricing information, customer lists and volumes are confidential and shall not be disclosed to any third party except to subcontractors who are bound by equivalent obligations or where required by law.

8. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY
Neither party shall be liable for indirect, consequential or pure economic loss, loss of profit, loss of business or loss of anticipated savings, howsoever arising. The Provider's aggregate liability arising out of or in connection with the agreement in any contract year shall not exceed the greater of the fees paid in the preceding six months or two million rupees, except in respect of death or personal injury caused by negligence, fraud or wilful misconduct, liability which cannot be excluded at law, or breach of confidentiality, in respect of which there is no cap.

9. TERMINATION
Either party may terminate for convenience on ninety days written notice, subject to payment of a demobilisation charge covering the cost of winding down. Either party may terminate for material breach on thirty days written notice where the breach is not remedied within that period. Termination does not affect accrued rights or any provision intended to survive, including clauses 6, 7 and 8.

10. FORCE MAJEURE
Neither party is in breach for a failure to perform caused by an event beyond its reasonable control, provided it notifies the other party within five business days and uses all reasonable endeavours to resume performance. If the event continues for more than sixty consecutive days either party may terminate on written notice without penalty.
question: What is the target order picking accuracy, what service credit applies when it is missed, and under what condition can the Client terminate immediately?
reference_answer: The target for order picking accuracy is ninety nine point five percent of order lines picked without error, measured monthly. For each full percentage point below target a service credit of one percent of that month's storage and handling charges applies, capped in aggregate at ten percent of those charges in any one month. The Client may terminate immediately on written notice without penalty if picking accuracy falls below ninety seven percent or dispatch on time falls below ninety five percent in any single month, or if either metric misses target in three consecutive months.
